races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Francophone
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two wins and three places from 15 similar-going starts; trainer Charlie Johnston at a respectable 4/52 in 14 days and Pierre-Louis Jamin riding — needs to secure a clean berth early given the crowded prominent group, and a recent run 14 days ago keeps fitness sharp.
runners_data.comment: Francophone arrives here just 14 days fresh, boasts going experience and a win in her last five starts, and our rating of 110 marks her out as a genuine threat; the worry is that her four subsequent efforts have been below that winning level.

runners_data.name: Miss Justice
runners_data.note: Headgear noted (ht); has place form at 12f on good but winless in last five starts; Brian Meehan's yard at 0/13 in 14 days is a cold stat, and from 28 days off she is not guaranteed to peak; naturally prominent but the traffic situation over 1m4f could compound a tendency to find little late.
runners_data.comment: Miss Justice has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 111 puts her among the strongest threats in this field — the risk is that she's been winless in her last five starts, suggesting a win may prove elusive again.

runners_data.name: Orchard Keeper
runners_data.note: Strong 14f specialist with a win and multiple places at this trip on good ground, returning from a lengthy 296-day absence for Roger Varian whose stable is in form (10/24 in 14 days); his instinct is to race forward but with the prominent slots full he is likely to be caught in midfield against his nature, and fitness after nearly a year off is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Placed third and a winner in her last five starts, but a 296-day absence is a significant query for Orchard Keeper; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a trainer striking at 42% offers some confidence, though the burden of 135 lb complicates matters.

runners_data.name: Orionis
runners_data.note: William Haggas horse with proven pace on good ground (10 from 12 similar-going runs); ran only 14 days ago so is fit and race-ready; naturally wants to race prominently but will likely find himself a position or two further back than ideal — Cieren Fallon's tactical awareness will matter here, and a clear passage into the Newmarket straight could allow his 12f class to tell.
runners_data.comment: Orionis arrives here just 14 days after finishing third, with a win three starts back and another five starts back underpinning her recent consistency; she has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 105 makes her a serious threat. The main risk is that seventh two starts back hints at vulnerability.

runners_data.name: Revoir
runners_data.note: Wears a visor; a consistent placer at 10-12f who has not won in recent outings, collecting four places without a win on good; Ralph Beckett has two runners today and this one is drawn into a tricky prominent battle — the headgear is an interesting addition but the 0W from 4P on similar ground suggests a confirmed runner-up profile.
runners_data.comment: Revoir has posted back-to-back seconds in recent starts and, rated 112 by us ahead of all nine rivals, she looks the one to beat here. Winless in her last five, she'll need to convert, but her experience over today's trip and going, combined with a 14-day freshener, sets her up well.

runners_data.name: Ryka
runners_data.note: True prominent type pushed to the back of the map through redistribution — her natural style is to race prominently, evidenced by wins over 10f and 12f; returning after 92 days and her last run on good went poorly (15th over 8f), so fitness and whether 14f suits off a long layoff are the real questions, not her position in the pace map.
runners_data.comment: Ryka won two starts back but hasn't run in 92 days, and her speed rating of 83 leaves her well short of where she needs to be on these figures, ranked seventh of nine. The distance and going hold no fears, but fitness is a real question mark.

runners_data.name: Gone By
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner; three-year-old carrying the 3lb allowance with wins at 11f and 12f on good — uncontested up front on this going is an ideal scenario; Charles Bishop rides for Ralph Beckett (his second runner here) and 32 days between runs suggests straightforward preparation; the only risk is the absence of real competition meaning the gallop becomes too leisurely.
runners_data.comment: Gone By arrives in decent nick with back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, but our rating ranks her eighth of nine runners, and that gulf to the principals is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Romantic Symphony
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby three-year-old with a win at 11f on standard and placed at 12f on good; Billy Loughnane in the saddle for a stable with a sharp 7/20 in 14 days; naturally prominent and should be competitive for the positions immediately behind Gone By — the step up to 14f for the first time is the one genuine question mark over his profile.
runners_data.comment: Romantic Symphony won two of her last four starts, including a victory three starts back, but was only fourth two starts back before rallying to finish second last time out; she has run over today's trip and going, though 44 days off and a rating of 95 suggest she sits just below the class leaders here.

runners_data.name: Sunshine Star
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden three-year-old who is lightly raced but has been placed twice at 10f; only one place from four similar-going starts and no win on this surface type; though he sits in midfield on the map, his actual instinct is to race prominently — Robert Havlin will need to find him an uncontested berth or his chance is compromised by racing against his natural style at a trip stretching him.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and her speed rating gives little encouragement, though the trainer is firing at 26% and she returns just 12 days after filling the runner-up spot last time out, with going experience also in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Gone By is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine presser to push the tempo, is likely to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f trip on good-to-firm ground. The prominent cluster is badly congested — Francophone, Miss Justice, Revoir, and Romantic Symphony all want to race close to the pace and will jostle for the four or five positions immediately behind Gone By, creating meaningful traffic danger around the 2-3f marker as they compress into the final turn. Orchard Keeper, Orionis, and Sunshine Star are natural prominent types redistributed into midfield because there simply is no room for all of them at the head of affairs; of those three, Orionis (William Haggas, proven on this going) and Orchard Keeper (veteran of this trip, strong course form) are most likely to actually secure a forward position if gaps open. A measured, front-to-finish gallop set by Gone By primarily favours horses who can travel comfortably just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — prominent hold-position types with a proven turn-of-foot on good ground will be best served, while true hold-up horses pushing from too far back will find the steady tempo insufficient to generate a meaningful late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gone By Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Gone By is allowed to dictate an uncontested, honest pace and the prominent bunch tracks without disruption.
scenarios.body: Gone By sets a measured rhythm from the front and the race unfolds at a comfortable gallop that rewards horses who can sit second or third and quicken off the turn; the prominent types who secure a clean position just behind the leader get first run on the straight and are hardest to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Suits Hold Position
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion produces early scrimmaging that pushes several runners wider and causes a brief pace injection.
scenarios.body: The jostling for the prominent positions burns energy from Francophone, Miss Justice and Revoir early, leaving the horse who settles most calmly just off the pace with the clearest passage into the straight; a smooth traveller who avoids the traffic benefits most from the late tactical sorting-out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the finishing straight becomes a sprint, allowing anything from off the pace to close.
scenarios.body: Gone By's uncontested lead risks becoming too dawdling, compressing the field and flattening differentials in the straight; however, true hold-up horses are scarce and most of the nominal rear-runners are redistributed prominent types, limiting how far back any credible closer actually travels.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse in Straight
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of competition for the lead produces an unsustainably slow early tempo that collapses in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Gone By, having led on a very light rein, ties up late and the race degenerates into a bunched finish where minor positional advantages at the 1f pole prove decisive; this is an unlikely shape given Good to Firm conditions that encourage horses to quicken cleanly rather than grind.

watchPoints.text: Gone By's early fractions will set the entire race shape — if Charles Bishop allows her to coast in front unchallenged, watch for the pace to be deceptively slow and the finish to become a bunched sprint from 2f out.

The prominent cluster of Francophone, Miss Justice, Revoir, and Romantic Symphony all chasing the same three or four positions creates a high-traffic flashpoint 2-3f out — any rider who gets squeezed or blocked at that point effectively loses the race.

Orchard Keeper returns from 296 days off — Roger Varian's strong 14-day strike rate is encouraging, but a horse racing out of its natural role after such a long absence is a significant risk factor if he cannot find a prominent berth early.

Romantic Symphony is stepping up from 12f to 14f for the first time — if the trip stretches him in the final furlong, the horses who have proven stamina at this distance (Orchard Keeper, Miss Justice) will overhaul him close home.

Ryka's redistribution note — she is shown at the rear of the pace map but is a natural prominent racer; if she breaks smartly and David O'Meara has her primed after 92 days off, she could end up further forward than the map suggests, which would tighten the prominent battle further.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Love A Giggle
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 93, K.R. Burke sends her 45 days fresh with a strong record of 1-1-2 on similar Good/Good To Firm ground; races prominently and will be competitive if the pace battle softens the leaders ahead of her.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins highlight Love A Giggle's recent form, and she has run over today's distance and going before. Carrying 135 lb from stall five on a 45-day return, that latest unplaced run is the only minor blemish on an otherwise compelling recent profile.

runners_data.name: Acclamation Star
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon is a significant booking for James Owen, but her best form came on Firm rather than Good and her two runs on Good ground resulted in finishes of 6th and 10th, making the surface a mild concern despite her prominent style.
runners_data.comment: Acclamation Star won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with her trainer firing at 36% in the last fortnight — a potent combination; the concern is two unplaced efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Glamorize
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's mount has won twice and placed on all four runs on Good to Soft ground, runs prominently with a hood, and arrives just 11 days after her last start; the 6f trip is unproven but the evidence on similar ground is compelling.
runners_data.comment: Glamorize arrives in sparkling form, winning two of her last four starts including back-to-back victories, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; the weight of 131 lb from stall eight is the factor to watch.

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell partnering a horse with two wins on this course at this trip on Good ground is the most obvious pace-setter credential here; T14 of just 1/13 for Tate is the only notable concern, though the horse's individual form is very strong.
runners_data.comment: Havana Sprite arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience of both today's trip and going, making her a formidable threat from stall one carrying 130 lb; the main risk is whether 37 days off the track has blunted her sharp edge.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Soft last time and has placed over 5f on Good, but Richard Hannon's runner carries the lowest weight of the confirmed runners and may need the longer trip and this quicker surface to click together.
runners_data.comment: Rollthedicebaby arrives on the back of an unplaced effort last time out, though she was a winner two starts back and second three starts back, showing she retains ability; experience over today's trip and going is a plus, but that recent dip gives pause.

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: Two wins from her last two runs both came over 6f on Good ground, making her form directly relevant; Ollie Pears is 2/11 over 14 days and the 5-pound claimer Tom Kiely-Marshall could be a concern with four confirmed front-runners fighting for the same position.
runners_data.comment: Lady Dublin arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, yet her speed rating of 68 leaves her vulnerable against stronger company, and being ranked sixth of nine suggests she faces a stiff test of her current form.

runners_data.name: Donegal Rose
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good ground but finished 5th on her 5f debut and 4th over 7f last time, suggesting the 6f trip is her optimum; J F Egan is an upgrade in the saddle but the Hugo Palmer yard is only 4/29 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Donegal Rose is hard to fancy at these weights despite a win two starts back; she has run over today's trip and going, but a fourth last time out and a lowly speed rating of 70 leave plenty to prove here.

runners_data.name: Fire Thunder
runners_data.note: Won her latest start over 6f on Good and has placed in three of four outings over the same conditions; Marco Botti's filly is a consistent front-runner who will compete for the early lead, but faces stiff competition for that position from higher-rated rivals.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Fire Thunder faces a stiff task, though she arrives in good heart — a win last time out following three consecutive seconds — and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Showed a win and three places from six runs on Good/Good To Firm in her hist; a natural prominent racer, she has been mapped to a rear position given the field's pace saturation, and with a 7-pound claimer up and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.87, her chance is tempered by the likelihood she won't find her natural position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and unplaced last time out, Holi Scarlett faces a stiff ask here, though she does have experience over today's trip and going, and a win three starts back shows she can find the line.

races.paceDynamic: The going report confirms Good To Firm conditions for this 6f contest, meaning the surface will be quick and unforgiving of errors in positioning. Havana Sprite, Lady Dublin, Donegal Rose, and Fire Thunder all want to lead or race prominently, creating a near-certain strong early gallop from the gates — this is not a race where anyone will dictate unchallenged. The pace battle between these four will stretch the field out rapidly, putting a premium on stamina and the ability to maintain momentum into the final two furlongs rather than quicken from a standing start. With Holi Scarlett redistributed to a hold-up position despite being a natural prominent racer, the field holds more speed types than can all secure their preferred berth, with Havana Sprite and Lady Dublin — both proven course-and-distance performers at 6f on good ground — best equipped to establish early position; the tactical verdict strongly favours hold-up or late-finishing profiles that can exploit the scramble up front, or a high-class prominent runner with enough cruising speed to settle just off the burn and pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way battle for the lead burns too fierce in the first two furlongs, setting a pace that leaves the leaders vulnerable from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: Havana Sprite, Lady Dublin, Donegal Rose and Fire Thunder fight for supremacy and tie each other up, with the fractions unsustainable on Good To Firm ground over 6f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, One Leader Clears
scenarios.trigger: If one lead horse — most likely Havana Sprite or Lady Dublin — gains a tactical advantage early and controls the gallop without burning excess reserves.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner establishes a comfortable lead while the others are squeezed out behind them, allowing a metronomic gallop that suits the most efficient traveller at pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent type settles just off the contested lead and produces a decisive run two furlongs out when the pace leaders start to weaken.
scenarios.body: Love A Giggle or Glamorize, both proven prominent runners on Good To Firm, track the early skirmish and have energy preserved to quicken decisively inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Steals In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely suicidal and the field fans wide in the straight, creating a ground-save opportunity for the deepest held-up runner.
scenarios.body: Holi Scarlett, though not a natural hold-up type and operating out of role, is the only runner mapped to the rear and could benefit if chaos ahead is severe enough to present a clear late run.

watchPoints.text: Havana Sprite, Lady Dublin, Donegal Rose and Fire Thunder will all attempt to lead from the gates — monitor the draw and early positioning closely, as any barging or crowding in the first furlong could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.
Love A Giggle arrives 45 days fresh and has never run over 6f; if the trip stretches her stamina on Good To Firm ground, she may find the closing stages difficult despite her superior OR rating.

Holi Scarlett's jockey Olivia Haines (7lb claimer) faces an unusual tactical problem — the horse is a natural prominent type forced to the rear by pace saturation, and a jockey with limited experience may struggle to adapt in running.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this race despite the headline going listed as Good — expect fast fractions and watch whether any horse drawn wide is forced to use early energy to close gaps against the pace.

Glamorize runs just 11 days after her last start and wears a hood; watch her in the prelims and early on as a quick turnaround combined with headgear can occasionally produce an over-keen early performance that undermines her late kick.

races.name: Lodge At The National Stud Ebf Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Saxony
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old has won twice over 7f on Good ground this season and is the natural pace-setter here; the uncontested lead is a significant asset, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caveat on her ability to fully dominate if the field compresses around her.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Saxony shaped well when second two starts back and was a winner three starts back, so he brings genuine recent form to this; he has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating has him narrowly top of the field — the fourth last time out is the one to overcome.

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: William Haggas has a solid 14-day strike rate and Cieren Fallon rides, giving this horse strong connections — it has posted consistent placed efforts over 7f on Good ground — but its front-running instincts will be tested by a crowded prominent contingent, and it is unlikely to get the handy berth it prefers today.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts — second last time out, and a second two starts back — Hardy's Hero has run over today's trip and going and returns fresh on just nine days' rest; the main concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Mali
runners_data.note: Boasts a fine recent record over 7f on Good ground with two wins in five starts at this trip, and James Fanshawe's horse arrives fresh off a 22-day break in decent order; naturally wants to race prominently, though with several others ahead of it in the pecking order for that position, it may find itself further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Lion Of Mali has winning form in recent starts — a winner two starts back — but that fifth three starts back hints at inconsistency, and ranked fifth of six on our figures he looks up against it here, despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Electrical
runners_data.note: Brian Toomey's hold-up type has a modest form string in this grade and recent runs over longer trips on Good ground have produced finishing positions of 7, 6, 7 — coming from the rear requires a much stronger pace than looks likely in a six-runner field with one genuine front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of mid-to-rear finishes making him hard to fancy here, Electrical has at least run over today's trip and going before and carries a manageable 122 lb from stall 2 — though he has plenty to find on our figures as the lowest-ranked runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Tryst
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old won over this exact course, distance and going on its most recent start and Billy Loughnane rode it that day; the switch back from trips of 10f to 7f looks a positive return to its optimum, and a hold-up or late-pressing style suits this race shape if the pace holds up through the straight.
runners_data.comment: Tryst arrives on the back of a win last time out and with experience of today's distance and going, making her a clear danger here; the concern is whether she can bounce back from a dip in form — sixth and seventh in the two starts before that victory.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's filly has won twice at 7f on Good ground and was placed at 6f on this course, arriving here in excellent recent form with three wins from five; prominent in style and likely to secure a forward position behind Spirit Of Saxony, she is tactically well placed for the most probable race shape.
runners_data.comment: Sierra Sands arrives in fine nick, a winner on each of his last two starts and with experience of today's trip and going — the 22-day break looks just right, and his 134 lb burden is the only query for the progressive colt from stall three.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Saxony is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop over this 7f trip on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. Hardy's Hero and Lion Of Mali are both natural prominent racers but cannot all hold that position simultaneously — Spirit Of Saxony is most likely to secure the rail and the lead, with Sierra Sands the next most credible to press or sit just off the pace given her recent course-and-distance winning form. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, with Hardy's Hero and Lion Of Mali the ones most likely to be shuffled back from their preferred position. A controlled, single-file tempo over this straight 7f track will reward horses that can sit within striking range and produce a sustained finish — the prominent-to-midfield profile racing just off a comfortable lead is the most favoured tactical slot in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Saxony dictates an uncontested pace and the field settles into a single-file rhythm from the outset.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Saxony gets an uncontested lead at a fair clip on Good to Firm ground, saving enough for the straight, and the race becomes a test of sustained galloping ability over the final two furlongs; horses racing in close attendance off a manageable pace are ideally positioned to pounce. Sierra Sands, with her strong recent 7f course form and prominent style, and Tryst, who won over this trip and going last time, are best placed to pick up the pieces if Spirit Of Saxony ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Saxony goes too hard early — even uncontested — and burns herself out inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected pace, even set by one horse, can gut the field on Good to Firm ground over 7f, leaving the door open for hold-up horses to reel in the weakening leader through the final furlong. Tryst and Lion Of Mali, if they find their rhythm further back, would be best positioned to come home strongest in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Scrappy Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy's Hero and Lion Of Mali push for position early and force a more pressured pace than Spirit Of Saxony wants.
scenarios.body: If the prominent types jostle for position in the early stages, the tempo rises and the race becomes a true test of stamina-plus-speed over the 7f, stretching the field and nullifying any horse that has used energy to secure position. Sierra Sands, who has the fitness and course form to handle a stronger pace, and Tryst as the closers' beneficiary, would emerge as the likeliest beneficiaries in this more truly run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and sustained and the field strings out, leaving Electrical or Tryst with a clear run from the rear.
scenarios.body: A truly run race over 7f on fast ground can theoretically suit genuine hold-up horses closing off a strong gallop, but Electrical's recent form figures make this a low-probability winning scenario. Tryst is the more credible of the two hold-up types given her OR of 87 and a recent 7f win on Good ground, but this shape requires everything to go right for the backmarkers.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Hardy's Hero or Lion Of Mali push aggressively for a prominent position in the first two furlongs — if either forces the issue against Spirit Of Saxony, the tempo will spike and dramatically alter the race shape.

Sierra Sands has won twice going right-handed recently but her course form at Newmarket's straight July track reads well — monitor whether she settles cleanly behind the leader, as any traffic trouble from her forward position would be costly.

Tryst steps back sharply in trip from 10f to 7f after her win last time — if she comes here short of peak fitness or struggles to find her rhythm in the early stages of a six-runner field, her late challenge may arrive too late on this straight track.

Spirit Of Saxony was beaten at odds-on over this trip on Good ground last time out, suggesting her front-running dominance is not guaranteed — watch the early stalls to see whether she jumps cleanly and immediately assumes the lead without any challenge.

The going is reported Good to Firm throughout the card, which is faster than the headline Good described for this race — note whether any horse appears to be working harder than expected on the firmer surface in the middle stages of the race.

races.name: Racing Welfare Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with solid 1m2-1m4f form for Mark Loughnane, returning after 185 days off — the layoff is the key concern, though it has won fresh before; sits naturally prominent and should secure a position just behind Way Of Life, making it one of the better-placed runners in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Haku landed a win three starts back and was third two starts back, showing he retains the class to trouble the principals, and he has experience over today's trip to boot — the sole concern is whether 185 days off the track has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Way Of Life
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's eight-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the race and will likely be uncontested on the lead; similar-going form reads 0 wins from 4 attempts over comparable conditions, and racing a step up from 10-11f to 1m4f is a mild stamina query despite its stamina-slanted style.
runners_data.comment: Way Of Life brings strong recent form — a winner two starts back and third last time out — with distance and going experience counting in his favour. Carrying 135 lb is the one query, but at 15 days fresh he arrives in good order.

runners_data.name: Sixpack
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides this in-form six-year-old who has won twice at 1m4f on Good and Soft for James Owen, a trainer firing at 36% over 14 days; headgear noted (previously worn), and the hold-up style is a genuine fit for this race shape — the strongest stamina profile in the race on paper.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures and his speed rating of 77 gives little hope, but Sixpack does bring distance and going experience, a last-time-out fourth notwithstanding a hot recent sequence that includes three wins in his last six starts, and a trainer firing at 36%.

runners_data.name: Arqoob
runners_data.note: Lucy Wadham's eight-year-old has placed at 1m4f on Good ground before but form has been modest recently (three consecutive 4th-6th finishes); the hood is worn, Jack Mitchell takes the ride, and the prominent style is likely to see it travel kindly though it must find more late to feature.
runners_data.comment: Arqoob has been consistently competitive in recent starts, finishing third last time out and showing enough in his last five to pose a clear threat here — he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 91 gives him strong claims; the risk is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Greek Order
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's six-year-old comes into this off a string of 4th-6th finishes over 8-10f on Good ground — this 1m4f trip is a significant step up and his true racing instinct is to race up with the pace, though the congestion of prominent types means he is likely to be held up against his will.
runners_data.comment: Greek Order has been running without threatening in recent starts, and his rating of 95 — topping this eight-runner field — underlines his claims; he has experience on today's going and returns fit after 33 days. The risk is a trainer firing at just 5% in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: William Haggas enters a horse with consecutive 3rds at 1m3-1m4f and genuine course form at this trip; naturally forward-going but pressed into midfield by the density of prominent horses, meaning Cieren Fallon will need to make a move earlier than ideal if he is to deliver the horse's best.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in his last two outings, Divine Knight arrives in decent nick after 21 days off and has experience of today's going, though winless in his last five starts and carrying 130 lb, he faces a stiff task to break that duck here.

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's four-year-old arrives on a 10-day turnaround after winning over 10f on Good ground, which is an eye-catching angle given Prescott's precision with his horses; stepping up sharply in trip from 10f, and racing from the rear, so stamina confirmation over 1m4f is the outstanding question.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and his speed rating lags behind, making him hard to fancy despite a win last time out; he has run over today's going before and the trainer is in excellent recent form.

runners_data.name: First Officer
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's seven-year-old has placed in four of its last five at 1m2-1m4f on Good ground and is consistent, but its front-running inclinations are naturally suppressed in this field; Alexandra Egan claims 7lbs which helps the weight, but finishing its race from a position it does not want to race from will be a challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, First Officer has nonetheless finished second twice in recent outings and has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that our rating has him sixth of eight, suggesting he may need others to disappoint.

races.paceDynamic: Way Of Life is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course over 1m4f, will likely bowl along at a measured, uncontested tempo — no rival has the natural inclination or mandate to chase and pressurise. Haku and Arqoob are the genuine prominent types likely to settle just off the lead in the first and second slots behind Way Of Life, leaving Greek Order, Divine Knight, and First Officer — all natural prominent racers — squeezed into a midfield berth they will not relish. This field contains more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate; of those redistributed, Haku is best placed to actually secure a position near the pace given its proven stamina and course experience, while Greek Order (stepping markedly up in trip from 8-10f) and First Officer are the most likely to be shuffled back against their will. A sustainable, uncontested gallop set by Way Of Life on fast ground over this marathon trip strongly favours hold-up finishers with proven stamina who can pick up from off the pace — Sixpack and Almekarem are the profiles the race shape most naturally rewards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Way Of Life Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Way Of Life bowls along unchallenged and sets an honest but controlled pace that fails to stretch the field until the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Way Of Life sets every fraction, and the race develops into a true stamina test in the final quarter-mile where those with genuine 1m4f+ form over Good to Firm ground assert; hold-up horses with proven two-mile form get first run off the steady-ish tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses get a clean run through to deliver their challenges in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sixpack, with multiple wins at this trip on Good and Good to Firm, and Almekarem, fresh off a recent win at 10f, pick their way through tiring rivals late; the fast ground on the July course enables a powerful late surge from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too dawdling and those pushed into midfield — particularly Divine Knight or First Officer — manage to recover ground early enough to position prominently.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early gallop compresses the field and rewards those who steal forward to prominent positions mid-race; Divine Knight's trainer William Haggas has the ammunition to prep a horse to fire fresh, and First Officer's consistent 2/3-placed form at this trip could see it grind past a fading leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Way Of Life is never headed, bowling along at a crawl before quickening late on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: Way Of Life, who has won twice over this sort of trip and trips up on stamina, is never pressured and simply outstays rivals who cannot quicken on good ground after a tactical race; Haku, sitting just behind, is next best positioned to pounce.

watchPoints.text: Way Of Life (Olivia Tubb, 5lb claim) is likely to control the tempo completely unchallenged — if she gets a soft lead and quickens from the front on Good to Firm ground, this shape tilts sharply against hold-up horses who need a strong pace to close.

Sixpack carries the headgear flag and has won multiple times at this exact trip and distance type — monitor whether Billy Loughnane is able to get a clean passage from the rear in the straight, as traffic could be the deciding factor for the most qualified stayer in the field.

Greek Order, Divine Knight, and First Officer are all natural prominent racers crammed into midfield by the race shape — watch in the early stages for any of them forcing their way forward, which would inject pace and change the race entirely.

Almekarem is on a very quick 10-day turnaround for Sir Mark Prescott, who is notoriously precise with his runners — the sharp prep angle deserves respect even if the step up from 10f to 1m4f means stamina is unproven at this longer trip.

The going is confirmed Good to Firm for this 3:58 race at Newmarket July, which the race-day reports consistently state — fast ground benefits prominent and front-running types on the July course's long straight, adding a secondary layer of pressure on pure hold-up horses who need more fractions to close.

races.name: National Stud Fillies' Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Food For Thought
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has won twice at 10f on Good ground and confirmed her front-running credentials with a recent victory 21 days ago; she carries top weight at 135lbs but is clearly the controlling influence and this uncontested lead scenario is where she is most dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a winner two starts back, Food For Thought arrives in fine recent nick after 21 days off, with experience of both today's trip and going working in her favour at 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Thaluna
runners_data.note: William Haggas's filly steps up significantly in trip from her recent 7-8f efforts, and Cieren Fallon's booking is a strong positive indicator; her placed record on Good ground is solid but she will need to prove the 1m2f trip suits before she can be fully trusted, making her a prominent player with a question mark over stamina.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's hold-up filly has form at 10f on Good ground including a second, but in a field where the lone front-runner is likely to control a measured pace, she faces the classic problem of needing something she is unlikely to get; Billy Loughnane will need to be creative positionally to give her any chance of landing a blow.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last four starts, Hollywell Stream brings solid each-way claims here, has experience over today's trip and going, and arrives fresh after 24 days off; the risk is she remains yet to win in recent starts, so converting that consistency is the test.

runners_data.name: Valkyrie Storm
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground at 8f give Eve Johnson Houghton's filly strong current form credentials, and the quick 12-day turnaround suggests she is in a purple patch; Charles Bishop takes over in the saddle and she has the OR headroom from 75 to exploit, though stepping from 8f to 10f is the key question she must answer.
runners_data.comment: Valkyrie Storm won back-to-back races four and five starts back and returns on a sharp 12-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going in her favour; the worry is that she's been beaten in each of her last three outings since.

races.paceDynamic: Food For Thought is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of just four, and with Thaluna and Valkyrie Storm likely to track prominently rather than challenge for the lead, she should be able to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop around the July Course's sweeping 1m2f trip. Good To Firm ground (confirmed by the going report) rewards accurate, rhythm-based travelling, and a single pace-setter setting a measured tempo over this trip will likely produce a slowly-run-feeling race that strings out without ever truly punishing the leader. Closers like Hollywell Stream will need a meaningful injection of pace to be produced late, which a lone uncontested leader rarely provides in a four-runner field. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent-racing profile — horses that can travel close to the leader, avoid the traffic non-issue, and pounce in the final two furlongs rather than needing a genuine end-to-end gallop to reel in a tiring field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clear Win
scenarios.trigger: If Food For Thought settles into an uncontested rhythm and the prominent trackers fail to apply meaningful pressure before the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Food For Thought dictates her own fractions across the July Course's flat, galloping terrain, reaching the rising ground into the final furlong with enough in reserve to hold on; her two wins at this trip on Good ground confirm the combination suits her perfectly. Thaluna, travelling prominently off her shoulder, is the most likely beneficiary if Food For Thought ties up, but without a forcing pace to galvanise the closers, this shape most rewards those at the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Thaluna or Valkyrie Storm track Food For Thought closely and produce the sharper turn of foot entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: One of the prominent trackers sits a length off the leader travelling smoothly, draws alongside at the two-furlong marker and goes past before Food For Thought can respond; Cieren Fallon's tactical intelligence on Thaluna is particularly relevant given her placed record at 7-8f on Good ground and her step up to 1m2f suggesting a stayer's profile emerging. Valkyrie Storm's recent back-to-back wins on Good ground at 1m also leave her with claims if she gets a good tow into the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Off Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Food For Thought goes too fast or the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for Hollywell Stream.
scenarios.body: Hollywell Stream would need a genuine tempo to close into — her hold-up style over 10f on Good ground produced a second last time, but in a race where only one horse dictates a sustainable gallop, the required gap for a late run is unlikely to materialise in time. Billy Loughnane would need to get surprisingly close to the pace early to make this viable, and Jane Chapple-Hyam's 14-day strike rate of 2/12 tempers expectations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If all four runners bunch mid-race and the race becomes a sprint finish off a crawl.
scenarios.body: A field of just four with a lone front-runner rarely produces a genuine pace collapse, but if Food For Thought is ridden conservatively and the prominent pair refuse to commit, the final furlong could see all four within a length; in that scenario, the horse with the best raw speed and freshest legs — likely Valkyrie Storm on her quick turnaround and strong recent form — could pip the field in a dash. This is the least likely shape and depends on an unusually passive ride from Rhys Clutterbuck.

watchPoints.text: Food For Thought sets the entire tactical agenda — if Rhys Clutterbuck is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, the race could be over as a contest turning for home with three furlongs left.

Thaluna's step up from 7-8f to 1m2f is untested — if she fails to see out the trip she could stop quickly inside the final furlong having tracked the leader throughout, opening the door for Valkyrie Storm.
Valkyrie Storm's 12-day turnaround is notably quick for a three-year-old filly; if she is not fully wound up she risks flashing her finishing kick too early and emptying before the line.

With only four runners on a flat, galloping track, positional moves will happen early — watch the first two furlongs closely to see whether Thaluna or Valkyrie Storm immediately challenges Food For Thought for the lead or settles into a clear tracking role, as that will define the entire race shape.

races.name: British Racing School Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with seven runs at similar going yielding a win and five places; Chloe Lyons claims 7lbs, which matters at this level, but Merrimack ran just five days ago and that quick turnaround combined with a rear-tracking style on a flat 5f Newmarket straight is the key tactical concern.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in recent starts, Merrimack brings solid placed form — third last time out, and a runner-up two starts back — and he has run over today's trip and going before; the five-day turnaround looks sharp enough, and our rating of 74 makes him an appealing proposition at 139 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Silky Robin
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 5f and 6f on Good ground give this five-year-old strong claims, and the 40-day break is not a worry given trainer Brian Toomey sends horses fresh; blinkers fitted, likely to race prominently and use natural speed to track Sound And Vision into the race — the most straightforward profile in the field.
runners_data.comment: Silky Robin arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious threat here; the main concern is whether 40 days off has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Point
runners_data.note: Shaped well when second over 5f on Good going and William Carson is a competent handler at Newmarket; the tongue tie and cheekpieces suggest connections are still working out the optimal setup, and four finishes outside the first three in recent starts keep expectations measured.
runners_data.comment: Tuscan Point arrives here on a quick 15-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions, and his second and win in recent starts demonstrate he can find the frame; the worry is he's shown inconsistency since, and that run of modest finishes will need reversing under 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Sound And Vision
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner with a style-fit score of 0.93, suggesting it is operating slightly outside its most natural role in this configuration; one win from six at similar going is modest, but setting the pace uncontested on Good to Firm at Newmarket's July course with Billy Loughnane aboard is a compelling tactical scenario regardless.
runners_data.comment: Sound And Vision arrives here fresh off a promising third last time out, and she was a winner three starts back, bringing winning form into this contest. She has experience over today's trip and going, but her fifth two starts back is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Dottie Diamond
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins including two at 5f on Good going mark Dottie Diamond as a horse in fine form, but its natural hold-up style means it sits further back than its race record might suggest; Jack Mitchell will need a clean run in a small field to deliver from off the pace, and the style-fit tag is a genuine dampener.
runners_data.comment: Dottie Diamond arrives on the back of three consecutive wins and is fit from just 11 days ago, with experience of today's trip and conditions — genuine positives. However, she ranks fifth of six on our figures, making her hard to fancy against stronger-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: No wins from seven runs at similar going conditions and the youngest and most lightly-weighted runner here at OR 55; a natural hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the crowded rear of this field, and Cieren Fallon will need things to fall perfectly for a horse still finding its feet at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a ninth two starts back her worst recent effort, Angel Summer arrives just five days after her latest sixth — quick turnaround fitness is a mild plus, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked last on our figures she faces a stiff task from stall one.

races.paceDynamic: Sound And Vision is the lone confirmed front-runner on a flat, straight 5f at Newmarket (July) on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine rival willing to press them from the gates, they are set to control tempo from the off at a pace that suits rather than destroys. Silky Robin will track closely in a prominent position, creating a two-horse early contest for the lead quarter, while Merrimack, Tuscan Point, Dottie Diamond, and Angel Summer are all hold-up types who will need something to chase — a scenario that favours pace on this unrelenting track. The field holds more hold-up and midfield types than the race shape can naturally accommodate; Dottie Diamond and Angel Summer, both genuine closers, are unlikely to find the wide-open gaps that a larger, truly contested race would provide, and it is Sound And Vision and Silky Robin who are most likely to actually secure the positions they need. This race shape decisively favours prominent runners who can control sectionals and maintain momentum to the line, with those forced to come from behind facing an uphill task on a flat, fast course that rarely forgives passengers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds Firm
scenarios.trigger: If Sound And Vision dictates a measured, uncontested tempo and Silky Robin cannot make a serious challenge to the front
scenarios.body: Sound And Vision rolls along in front without pressure, preserving energy for the final furlong where their Good-going form (3rd on similar) and Billy Loughnane's confident handling see them hold on; Silky Robin, prominent throughout and fresh from back-to-back wins including a 5f win on Good, is ideally placed to strike if anything goes wrong ahead

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Silky Robin pushes forward early and genuinely contests the lead with Sound And Vision, creating a two-horse duel
scenarios.body: A contested early pace raises the tempo enough to bring the race to life for those sitting a length or two off the pace, but Silky Robin's recent sharp form (5-1-1 last six) and proven 5f turf ability on Good ground makes them the natural beneficiary of the fight; Sound And Vision, racing in a slightly unnatural role per the style-fit tag, may fade marginally if the pace truly quickens

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and the front pair burn each other off, leaving a gap for a closer
scenarios.body: Merrimack, with solid consistent form at 5f on Good going (3rd, 2nd, 3rd in recent similar conditions) and seven runs at similar going producing a win and five places, is the best-credentialled closer to capitalise; Dottie Diamond has the raw form (four wins from nine on similar going, three consecutive wins) but the redistribution note and style-fit tag means securing a meaningful run from the back in a six-runner field is far from guaranteed

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If market leaders underperform and Angel Summer or Tuscan Point produce career-best efforts
scenarios.body: Tuscan Point has shown 5f Good-going ability (2nd and 4th in recent outings) and William Carson rides well at the course, so a forward move from a clean draw could catch the field flat-footed; Angel Summer, however, has no wins on similar going in seven attempts and is still learning the craft at three, making this the least probable outcome

watchPoints.text: Sound And Vision's draw and early stride length — if they jump cleanly and establish the lead within the first furlong, the race is almost certainly going to be run to their strengths and the closers will have a mountain to climb on fast Newmarket ground.

Silky Robin's early intent — if Joe Leavy sends them forward aggressively from the gates rather than sitting second, the pace dynamic shifts from controlled to contested and the entire probability landscape changes significantly.

Dottie Diamond's starting position and early traffic — in a field of only six, Jack Mitchell must avoid being squeezed or checked in the first two furlongs or the hold-up style becomes redundant at 5f where there is simply no time to recover lost ground.

Merrimack's recovery from five days ago — watch the market move; if Chloe Lyons gets a positive push in betting, it suggests the quick turnaround is considered a non-issue by Stuart Williams' yard, but a flat or drifting price tells the opposite story.

Ground confirmation at the track — the going report consistently shows Good to Firm for this race across all readings; any last-minute softening toward Good would most benefit the hold-up types like Dottie Diamond and Merrimack who need the pace to be truly strong.
